risk_reasons: The edited call site is worker/jobs/response-generation/persist.ts, inside the response-persist transaction on the auto-approval path.
A defect in guard 4's off-arm re-opens #1079: a throw there aborts every generate_response persist while the kill switch is already off.
goal: While REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED is off, a policy_gate_held decision carrying a block reason absent from POLICY_GATE_HELD_REFUSAL_CATEGORIES raises its own operator signal naming that code, distinct from the ledger-dark warning.
non_goals: Changing the Restraint tab's ledgerRecording disclaimer or any read path.
Changing wouldRecordRefusal, noteRefusalLedgerDark, warnLedgerDisabled, or the once-per-episode ledger-dark latch.
Changing the guard 4 on-arm, which already reports a vocabulary fault through withLedgerAttribution.
Adding a signal to the held_draft lane or to worker/jobs/publisher/auto-policy-downgrade.ts.
Widening the Refusal ledger kill switch's containment guarantee, or making an unmapped code write a Refusal row.
user_visible_behavior: An operator sees a Sentry issue at level error, tagged subsystem=refusal_ledger and fault=unmapped_block_reason, naming every unmapped block reason, when the ledger is off and a held draft carries one.
The same event writes one logger line, so the fault survives a Sentry transport failure.
An operator can now tell 'the ledger is off deliberately' from 'the ledger is off and a vocabulary hole exists behind it', because the two carry different messages and different levels.
invariants: Guard 4's containment is by NON-EXECUTION: the new signal must not call resolvePolicyGateRefusal and must not throw.
Object.hasOwn is the only membership test used, because it cannot throw.
The new signal owns a separate latch. It never reads, writes, or resets warnedThisEpisode or nextWarnAttemptAt.
The ledger-dark warning still fires only when a row would genuinely have been written, so wouldRecordRefusal keeps its every-mapped-and-non-null form.
The two signals are mutually exclusive by construction: an unmapped member makes wouldRecordRefusal false.
src/lib/refusals/write.ts stays the single owner of every Refusal ledger signal transport; persist.ts stays a call site.
A throwing logger or a throwing Sentry never rejects the helper and never changes control flow.
edge_cases: Empty blockReasons: no unmapped member, so no signal. Unreachable at the call site because guard 2 returns first.
Every member mapped and non-null: no signal here; noteRefusalLedgerDark fires instead.
Veto-only set (every member maps to null): no signal from either helper.
Mixed set of one mapped non-null member and one unmapped member: the new signal fires, the ledger-dark warning does not.
Two or more unmapped members in one decision: one signal naming all of them, in input order.
A second, different unmapped code later in the same process: silent, because the latch is a single boolean. Accepted, since a map hole is systemic and one line sends the operator to the map.
Sentry.captureMessage throws synchronously: the latch stays unset and a cooldown of WARN_RETRY_COOLDOWN_MS delays the next attempt, mirroring warnLedgerDisabled.
logger.warn throws: swallowed, and the Sentry capture below it still runs.
The ledger is on: the new signal never runs, because guard 4's off-arm is its only call site.

rollback_plan: Revert the branch. The change adds one observability signal and no state, no schema and no control-flow branch, so a revert restores the prior behaviour exactly. REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED keeps its meaning either way.
observability: Sentry: level error, tags subsystem=refusal_ledger and fault=unmapped_block_reason, message naming the unmapped codes.
Worker log: one structured warn line carrying the same codes and the flag name.
Silence is the success state. The signal firing on staging or production means a block reason escaped the compiled AutoApprovalBlockReason union.
